what_it_does: Phoenix redesigns how GPUs and storage systems exchange data by eliminating an inefficient workaround. Normally, GPU Direct Storage (GDS) uses temporary host memory buffers to communicate with the Linux operating system, wasting resources and complicating deployment. Phoenix instead uses a modern Linux kernel feature (ZONE_DEVICE, available since Linux 4.3) to let the GPU's own memory appear directly in the system's virtual memory map, eliminating the intermediate buffers entirely. This improves input/output performance and reduces complexity.
